effort: Create hip-driven forward force and controlled hamstring contribution without adding a large ankle-rebound dose.
brief: The target is force from the hip behind the stance leg and active lower-leg recovery. E1 anchors a paused forward push. Split and single-leg takeoffs change leg contribution while preserving two-foot receiving. Offset swing and hinge-dominant release express hip force against light implements; rapid knee flexion addresses leg recovery. The primary hinge and knee-flexor strength roles receive priority while calf work is reduced.
marker: In each two-attempt set, record a true two-second pause before the forward push and a stable two-foot landing held for two seconds. Record re-dips and balance steps. Keep the modest distance/start depth comparable within the task; do not compare it with a countermovement or vertical jump.
review: Class 4 prescribed 23 bilateral landings and nine primary rounds with concentrated ankle work. Actual completion/recovery remain unknown. Class 5 uses only twelve planned landings, reduces bent-knee calf work to one set and temporarily omits the separate straight-knee calf role in favor of a supported hip-extension finish.
sequence: E1 comes first with the greatest isolated forward-push allocation. E2/E3 each use only two attempts per takeoff stance. E4–E6 have no flight; full recovery protects fast hip/knee action.

E.name: Paused Broad Jump to Stick
E.job: Main hip/leg force task: push forward from stillness without borrowing a countermovement.
E.cue: Hands on hips; hold a comfortable partial squat for 2 s, push a modest distance forward without re-dipping, land on both feet and hold 2 s. Reduce distance/start depth for lost control. No distance contest.

E.name: Split-Stance Forward Jump to Parallel Landing
E.job: Bias forward leg drive from a split stance while simplifying the finish to two parallel feet.
E.cue: Small stationary split stance; both feet push, travel a short distance forward and land with feet parallel beneath the body for 2 s. No leg exchange in flight. Shorten travel if pelvis twists or the back foot supplies nearly all the push.

E.name: Single-Leg Broad Jump to Two-Foot Landing
E.job: Isolate each leg's forward push without increasing the single-leg landing requirement.
E.cue: Stand on one foot, use a small dip and natural arms, push forward over a short controllable distance and place both feet underneath for a 2 s stick. Reduce distance for pelvic tilt or a reaching heel-first landing.

E.name: One-Arm Kettlebell Swing
E.job: Express hip extension against offset loading while resisting unwanted trunk rotation during the force transfer.
E.cue: Bilateral feet, light bell in one hand, no hand-to-hand release. Hinge and snap tall; bell floats below chest height. Park before changing arms. Reduce load if grip, shoulder lifting or rotation limits hip speed.

E.name: Hip-Hinge Medicine Ball Forward Toss
E.job: Emphasize rapid hip extension through a small fixed knee bend, contrasting with the earlier knee/hip scoop.
E.cue: Light ball low between thighs, knees softly bent and nearly steady. Hinge back, drive hips tall and release forward with both hands; feet stay grounded. No deep squat, back arch or return catch. Keep the flight low and contained.

E.name: Prone Band Leg Curl — fast concentric
E.job: Accelerate knee flexion for lower-leg recovery while keeping the hip/pelvis still.
E.cue: Prone on a comfortable floor, light band safely attached around the working ankle and a verified low fixed anchor beyond the feet. Flex knee quickly only toward 90°, return over 2 s. Keep thighs/pelvis grounded; reduce tension for hip lift or cramping. Secure attachment must not slip or snap toward the athlete.

S.name: Quadruped Bent-Knee Hip Extension
S.job: Light gluteal strengthening while controlling lumbar/pelvic motion before loaded hip extension.
S.cue: Hands/knees supported, one knee stays bent as that thigh moves backward only to trunk line. 2 s lift, 2 s return; no back arch or pelvic twist. Reduce range if the trunk changes shape; bodyweight only.

S.name: Supine Long-Lever Heel-Dig Isometric
S.job: Lightly load the hamstrings in a longer-knee position before the hinge/walkout work.
S.cue: Supine with knees softly bent and heels grounded well away from hips; press heels gently down/back without moving them or lifting the pelvis. Keep effort easy and breathing relaxed. Bring heels closer for cramping or strain; do not turn this into a maximal bridge hold.

P.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
P.cue: Soft knees, hips back, DBs close; lower 3 s and rise in 1 s. Stop the descent before back rounding; reduce load/range if the hinge becomes spinal movement.
P.job: Primary loaded hip-extension anchor for the day's hip-driven force emphasis.

P.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells at sides
P.cue: Floor split stance, front foot planted, pelvis square; lower 2 s and rise firmly for 1 s. Reduce load/range for collapse or balance loss. Use one DB with stable hand support instead of two unsupported DBs if needed; counts stay the same.
P.job: Retain knee/hip force from each stance leg alongside the hinge emphasis.

P.name: Glute Bridge Walkout
P.cue: Keep a floor bridge while four small alternating heel steps go out and four return; eight steps at about 1 s each = one full cycle. Choose reach so four cycles are challenging with 2–3 whole cycles available. Shorten reach for pelvic sag or cramping; do not add steps or cycles.
P.job: Prioritize challenging knee-angle hamstring control, distinct from the hinge and brief isometric preparation.

P.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated dumbbells
P.cue: Both legs together, knees near 90°, heels start on floor, hands secure DBs on lower thighs above knees. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s. Reduce load for bounce/lost heel height. If bench fit is unsuitable, use supported standing bent-knee calf raises instead, same reps/rest, and log changed knee angle.
P.job: Keep a small knee-flexed ankle-force exposure while reducing plantarflexor concentration.
P.decision: Class 4 2 × 8 → 1 × 8: planned redistribution away from ankle emphasis, not a response to invented soreness. Restore volume only with a relevant need and actual recovery.

P.name: Hip Thrust — dumbbell across pelvis
P.cue: Upper back on stable bench, feet planted, hands secure pelvic DB. Rise 1 s, hold 1 s, lower 2 s; finish ribs/pelvis aligned. Reduce load for lumbar arching. Use a loaded floor Glute Bridge instead if bench fit/stability fails, with the same dose/rest and changed support logged.
P.job: Add supported hip-extension finish force to complement the RDL's flexed-hip range.
P.decision: New 1 × 8 hip-thrust role replaces the straight-knee calf slot for this hip-focused class; select load through a light set, not prior-class assumptions.

P.name: Supine Band-resisted Hip Flexion
P.cue: Secure loop band around both forefeet; nonworking leg straight with heel grounded. Flex working hip/knee toward thigh-vertical in 2 s, hold 1 s, return 2 s without arching or moving the anchor heel. Reduce tension/range for pelvic tilt. If a secure loop is unavailable, use seated DB hip flexion instead with hands securing the DB above the knee: same dose/rest, small controlled thigh lift; preparation unloaded.
P.job: Maintain challenging thigh-recovery strength with a controlled pelvis.

equipment: E4 requires prior competent one-arm bell handling; use two-hand swings instead if needed, 1 × 8 total, same light fast intent and 90 s afterward, no flight. E5 requires an exclusive contained throwing/retrieval lane; use a light two-hand hip-hinge ball swing without release instead, 1 × 3 with 20 s resets and 90 s afterward, replacing three throws with three held-ball accelerations. For E6 without a verified safe band/anchor, use unresisted prone fast leg curls instead, same dose/tempo/rest; gravity/body-segment acceleration supplies the small rapid task without claiming equivalent resistance. No unlisted anchor is assumed available.
count_note: E1 four + E2 four + E3 four = twelve two-foot landing events, 24 individual foot contacts. E3's takeoff is unilateral but receiving is bilateral. Other default explosive work: eight offset swings, three hinge-dominant throws and eight fast knee curls. The hamstring hold is ten seconds total with both heels, not ten repetitions. No paired hip-hinge/scoop repetition is counted as two drills. Replacement throws and no-release swings must be logged separately.
novelty: The six default drills introduce a paused forward vector, split-to-parallel forward finish, single-leg forward push with shared receiving, offset bell loading, a hinge-only release and isolated rapid knee flexion. Several are declared relatives of prior vertical jumps/scoops/swings; their joint action, vector or force-sharing jobs change meaningfully. They are not counted as unrelated exercise families. The box-style seated takeoff was not repeated merely to fill an explosive slot.
audit: Reduced landings and calf sets while increasing hip/hamstring emphasis; retained only one hip-thrust and one walkout working set to limit overlapping posterior-chain fatigue. Limited rapid curls to four per leg and specified an unresisted replacement for unconfirmed anchor hardware. Rejected Nordic-drop/catch variations because the unknown cohort response does not justify that eccentric demand.
progression: Retain the RDL and split-squat prescriptions unless actual execution/effort warrants a load adjustment; no automatic increase. New swing/throw/curl conditions require demonstrated control at their small doses. Class 6 should consolidate pelvic control with modest lateral demands, not assume these hip-focused tasks were performed.
map_note: Hip/hamstring emphasis with twelve bilateral landings and reduced calf volume.
next_job: Pelvic control during small frontal or diagonal displacement, with low-impact consolidation.
handoff: Review Class 5, especially actual hip/hamstring recovery if supplied, then finalize Class 6 before proceeding further.

final_review: Checked posterior-chain overlap: only twelve two-foot landings, four walkout cycles and one hip-thrust set; calf volume is intentionally reduced. Rapid knee curls require a verified band attachment or the explicitly lower-resistance same-action replacement. Related jump/swing variants are disclosed. Unknown performance does not justify increasing loads or using Nordic drop/catch work.
